q-163049.name: Question 1
q-163049.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=xy-{y}^{3},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
q-163049.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-{y}^{3})=y, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-{y}^{3})=x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}(-1) & (2)-3(-1)^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-163049.html:
Question 1
?

For the transformation f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=xy−y3,x=[xy],

calculate f′ at a=[2−1].

a
[−11]
b
[1−1]
c
[11]
d
[1−1]
e
[−1−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(xy−y3)=y,∂f∂y=∂∂y(xy−y3)=x−3y2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[yx−3y2]

and f′ at a=[2−1] is

f′(a)=[(−1)(2)−3(−1)2]=[−1−1].

q-163045.name: Question 2
q-163045.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
q-163045.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=2x-y, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=-x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

q-163045.html:
Question 2
?

For the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=x2−xy+y2,x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[2y−x2x−y]
b
[2x−12y−1]
c
[2x−y−x+2y]
d
[2y−x−y+2x]
e
[2x−12y−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(x2−xy+y2)=2x−y,∂f∂y=∂∂y(x2−xy+y2)=−x+2y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[2x−y−x+2y].

q-162942.name: Question 3
q-162942.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz) \\ {x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & \frac{1}{z} \\ \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & {x}^{2}z & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
q-162942.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)=2xyz,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \frac{1}{y} & \frac{1}{z} \\ 2xyz & {x}^{2}z & {x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].
$$

q-162942.html:
Question 3
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[ln⁡(xyz)x2yz],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[1xAA1zAAx2zAA]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
x2y, 1z, and x2y
b
2xyz, 1z, and y2z
c
x2y, 1x, and x2y
d
2xyz, 1y, and yz
e
2xyz, 1y, and x2y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f1∂z∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f2∂z]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(ln⁡(xyz))=1x,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(ln⁡(xyz))=1y,∂f1∂z=∂∂z(ln⁡(xyz))=1z∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x2yz)=2xyz,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x2yz)=x2z,∂f2∂z=∂∂z(x2yz)=x2y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1x1y1z2xyzx2zx2y].

q-163099.name: Question 4
q-163099.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{y} \\ {e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
q-163099.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x-y})={e}^{x-y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x-y})=-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} \\ {e}^{x-y} & -{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

For the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[xyex−y],x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[1y−xy2ex−y−ex−y]
b
[1yex−y−xy2−ex−y]
c
[−xy21y2−yex−yxex−y]
d
[1y1y2ex−y−ex−y]
e
[1yxy2−ex−yex−y]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f2∂x∂f2∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(xy)=1y,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(xy)=−xy2∂f2∂x=∂∂x(ex−y)=ex−y,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(ex−y)=−ex−y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1y−xy2ex−y−ex−y].

q-163078.name: Question 5
q-163078.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}+xy,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
q-163078.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xy)=2x+y,\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy)=x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x+y & x\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=2,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-2=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
2+(-3)+(-2)=-3.
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=x2+xy,x=[xy].

If the tangent to f at a=[−21] is given by

z−∗=[∗∗]([xy]−[−21])

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
1
b
−7
c
−2
d
−3
e
−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(x2+xy)=2x+y,∂f∂y=∂∂y(x2+xy)=x

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[2x+yx].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[−21], we have

f(a)=2,f′(a)=[−3−2].

The tangent to f at x=a is given by

z−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

z−2=[−3−2]([xy]−[−21]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

2+(−3)+(−2)=−3.

q-163077.name: Question 6
q-163077.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1),\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
q-163077.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1} & \frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\operatorname{ln}⁡6,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\operatorname{ln}⁡6=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡6+(-\frac{1}{3})+\frac{2}{3}=\operatorname{ln}⁡6+\frac{1}{3}.
$$

q-163093.name: Question 7
q-163093.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{1})+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{2}+1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at  $a=[\begin{aligned}e \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}e \\ -1\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
q-163093.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{1})+{x}_{2})=\frac{1}{{x}_{1}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{1})+{x}_{2})=1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}^{2}+1)=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}^{2}+1)=2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{-1} & 1 \\ 0 & 2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}e \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-1} & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-1} & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}e \\ -1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+{e}^{-1}+(-2)={e}^{-1}-2.
$$

Question 7
?

Consider the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[ln⁡(x1)+x2x22+1],x=[x1x2].

If the linear approximation of f at a=[e−1] is given by

f(x)≈[∗2]+[∗10∗](x−[e−1]),

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
e−1−2
b
2e−1−2
c
2e−1+1
d
e−1−1
e
e−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(ln⁡(x1)+x2)=1x1,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(ln⁡(x1)+x2)=1∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(x22+1)=0,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(x22+1)=2x2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[x1−1102x2].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[e−1], we have

f(a)=[02],f′(a)=[e−110−2].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[02]+[e−110−2](x−[e−1]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

0+e−1+(−2)=e−1−2.

q-163162.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
q-163162.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2})=3{x}_{1}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2})=-1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}^{2} & -1 \\ {x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}} & {e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+(-1)+1=1.
$$
